evals.prompt: I want to apply for a Senior Product Manager role at Linear (the project management tool). I'm particularly interested in their developer experience team. I don't have my resume handy right now but I'm curious — can you run the company research stage first and show me what you find? I want to know if this is a company worth pursuing before I put in the effort.
evals.expected_output: Skill correctly identifies this as a Stage 1-only request. Asks for department confirmation (developer experience is mentioned). Runs web research on Linear and produces: (1) a narrative company brief with all six sections (inside scoop, mission, market position, product strategy, equity, interview intel), confidence labels on claims, recency tags, and representative employee review quotes; (2) a company-analysis JSON file. After presenting the brief, offers to proceed to cover letter and resume stages when resume/JD are ready.

evals.prompt: hey I'm trying to apply for a PM job and i have both my resume and the job description. company is called Notion, role is Group Product Manager - Enterprise. here are the files.
evals.expected_output: Skill asks for any personalization notes and confirms it will run all three stages. Runs Stage 1 (Notion company research with enterprise focus), presents narrative brief and JSON. Then runs Stage 2 pre-draft analysis — competitiveness ranking, strengths/risks for GPM Enterprise role specifically, positioning strategy. Asks for approval before writing cover letter. After letter is drafted, runs Stage 3 alignment table, gap questions, ATS keywords. Waits for gap answers before producing optimized resume. All outputs saved to a notion_gpm-enterprise/ folder.

evals.prompt: I only need the cover letter — I already did my own research on the company. The role is Head of Product at a Series B startup called Haystack (they make developer analytics software). My resume is attached and so is the job description. Can you just write me a good cover letter?
evals.expected_output: Skill acknowledges user wants only Stage 2. Offers to run Stage 1 briefly anyway (or asks if they want to share their research notes as context). Either way, proceeds with cover letter stage. Does the pre-draft analysis (competitiveness, strengths/risks, positioning) before writing. Asks for positioning approval. Produces a one-page letter grounded in the attached resume and JD, not generic filler. Explains its framing choices in the rationale section.
